reason: The cited evidence shows that nitriding can form hard nitrides and increase surface hardness in other alloys (E1), and that surface modifications on TC4 can improve hardness and wear resistance (E2). However, neither passage provides specific evidence for the proposed nitriding parameters on TC4, the formation of a nanocrystalline TiN layer, the exact mechanism of dislocation pinning, or the preservation of bulk ductility and fatigue performance.
premises: Nitriding can form hard nitride phases (e.g., TiN) on alloy surfaces, increasing hardness
Surface engineering (e.g., nitriding) can improve wear resistance of titanium alloys
A nanocrystalline TiN-rich layer can be produced on TC4 by gas nitriding at ~850°C for 4 hours
The TiN precipitates will act as dislocation obstacles and resist plowing, improving wear resistance
The nitriding treatment will not compromise the bulk ductility and fatigue performance of TC4
